rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> one-season (2019/20) split-plot RCBD field experiment at Werer with drip vs furrow as main plots and four ETc levels as subplots, three blocks. Q2: Results, 'Effects of irrigation system and irrigation level on water use efficiency' and Table 3 <U+2013> drip at 100% ETc gave 16666.6 kg/ha vs 7078.2 kg/ha for conventional furrow at 100% ETc; the text states this as a 57.53% yield increase over conventional furrow (farmers' practice).
rows.notes: Single field trial, one site, one crop, one season; yield measured by harvest only (one method). No soil-water or evaporation measurements reported as a mechanism (only yield components). Interaction with irrigation level is shown (drip at 55% ETc yields less than CFI) but authors do not state a requirement. Economic analysis recommends drip only for 'resource full' producers, but that is about adoption/profitability, not a condition for the yield effect. No limitations stated. Table 3 gives LSD and CV but no per-treatment SD/SE/CI; treated as not meeting Q9 (doubt noted).

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> own field experiment at Werer, 2019/20, drip vs furrow at four irrigation levels. Q2: Abstract and Results <U+2013> highest seasonal water requirement 701.7 mm under conventional furrow at 100% ETc; drip at 100% ETc stated to save 33.7% of irrigation water compared to conventional furrow irrigation (farmers' practice).
rows.notes: Water saving is derived from scheduled/applied irrigation depths computed from ETc and application efficiency, not from independent measurement of soil water or crop ET; single method, single site. No dispersion reported for water applied. Note the paper also reports that drip at 100% ETc used 24.58% more water than alternate furrow, so the saving is relative to conventional furrow only. No limitations or conditions stated.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> own split-plot field experiment at Werer, 2019/20. Q2: Results text and Table 3 <U+2013> drip at 100% ETc yielded 16666.6 kg/ha vs 4753.1 kg/ha for alternate furrow at 100% ETc; the text states a 71.5% maize yield increase over alternate furrow irrigation.
rows.notes: Same single-site, single-season, single-method trial as the other rows. The passage's second half (24.58% 'loss' of irrigation water over alternate furrow) actually means drip applied more water than alternate furrow; the crop_production claim itself is supported. No mechanism, scale, representativeness, limitations or dispersion beyond LSD/CV in Table 3.

notes: Full text available. Internal inconsistency: abstract says highest WUE (2.38 kg/m3) at drip 100% ETc while Table 3 and text give 2.38 at drip 85% ETc and 2.15 at 100% ETc. Results narrative is partly duplicated. Economic analysis (Table 4) is based on CIMMYT partial budget; no statistical uncertainty on it.
